issues.failure_explanation: The exact Gaussian product integral is \int_{\R^d} \hat\varphi((x-y)/\sigma)\hat\varphi((x'-y)/\sigma)dy = \sigma^d (\hat\varphi * \hat\varphi)((x-x')/\sigma) = \sigma^d 2^{-d/2}\hat\varphi((x-x')/(\sqrt{2}\sigma)) = \sigma^d (4\pi)^{-d/2} e^{-|x-x'|^2/(4\sigma^2)}. The display asserts instead the width 2\sigma (i.e. exponent -|x-x'|^2/(8\sigma^2), off by a factor of 2), drops the factor |D_1|^{-1}, and uses the constant 2^{-d} in place of 2^{-d/2}/|D_1|. The claimed equality is therefore false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final equality by the correct identity \frac{\sigma^{2s-d}2^{-d/2}}{|D_1|}\hat\varphi((x-x')/(\sqrt{2}\sigma)).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit covariance kernel identified with the GP method in the related-work comparison is wrong (kernel width off by \sqrt{2}, wrong constants). Only the qualitative takeaway (GP uses a Gaussian kernel with one fixed scale parameter) survives; no labelled result or other part of the paper uses this identity.
issues.title: Gaussian convolution identity in the GP-kernel comparison is computed incorrectly
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to a heuristic motivational display; no formal result, algorithm, or advertised guarantee depends on the erroneous formula, and the qualitative conclusion of the paragraph is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption assu:caratheodory only requires continuity of E(x,\cdot) and B(x,\cdot) for almost every x. On the exceptional null set the composition can fail to converge: e.g. a Carathéodory map with E(x_0,u) discontinuous in u at a single point x_0 and \cN\mu_k(x_0) converging to the discontinuity satisfies all hypotheses while \cE[\cN\mu_k](x_0) diverges. The proof therefore establishes convergence only for \nu_D-a.e. x in D and \nu_{\partial D}-a.e. x on \partial D, not for every x as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma with a.e. convergence (sufficient for every Fatou-type application), and for the empirical problem either strengthen Assumption assu:caratheodory to continuity in the state variables for every x, or require the collocation points to be chosen from the full-measure set of continuity points.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma overstates its conclusion. All Fatou-type uses (existence for the continuous problem, the limit step in thm:convergence) only need the a.e. version and are unaffected, but lower semicontinuity of the empirical loss requires convergence at the fixed collocation points, which may lie in the exceptional null set; hence existence of minimizers for the empirical problem (second half of thm:existence) is not established as written, and thm:representer, which cites thm:existence for a solution of the empirical problem, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Residual convergence lemma claims convergence for all x, but the Carathéodory assumption only gives convergence a.e.
issues.why_classification: The repair is a forced local weakening of the lemma plus a standard, locally checkable assumption tweak; all stated conclusions (existence for both problems, and the downstream representer theorem) survive with no change of method, rates, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The appendix (thm:added-1) proves B^s_{1,1}(\R^d) \hookrightarrow \cV(\R^d) only for the unrestricted dictionary \Omega = \R^d \times (0,1], whose representing measures are spread over all of \R^d, whereas the paper's space is defined with \Omega = D_1 \times (0,\sigma_{\max}] (centers restricted to a bounded neighborhood of D); no restriction, truncation, or extension argument linking the two is given, and truncation of the constructed measures to D_1 changes the represented function. Moreover, read literally on \R^d the first arrow is false: H^k(\R^d) \not\subset L^1(\R^d) \supset B^s_{1,1}(\R^d) for any k (e.g. smooth functions decaying like |x|^{-a}, d/2 < a \le d, lie in every H^k but not in L^1). On a bounded domain the first arrow holds for k > s, but then the appendix result does not apply. Under either reading the chain does not establish u \in \cV(D).

issues.failure_explanation: The paper never states any hypothesis on the coefficients c_i, b_i, A_i, d_i, e_i (not even boundedness or measurability), and the assumptions on \hat E, \hat B (Carathéodory slice boundedness, gradients bounded in x for each fixed l, C^{0,\gamma} in x) are not required to hold uniformly in l on bounded sets. Consequently, for v \in C^{2,\gamma}(\bar D) the composed residual x \mapsto \cR[v](x) need not be bounded or Hölder continuous: e.g. unbounded coefficients make \cL_E v unbounded, and one can construct \hat E satisfying all stated conditions (per-l bounded slices, per-l bounded x-gradients) with \hat E(x,l(x)) unbounded for a continuous l(x). Yet thm:convergence needs \cE[u^*]^2 bounded and measurable for the quadrature convergence and uniform boundedness of \hat L(u^*) (the step that bounds \|\mu_{K,\alpha}\| and yields limit points), and the bound \|\cR[v]\|_{C^{0,\gamma}} \le C\|v\|_\cV underlying eq:generalization and lem:added-1 requires C^{0,\gamma} coefficients and uniform Hölder/Lipschitz control, none of which is assumed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For fixed $\| e\|_{C^{0,\gamma}}$,
one can choose $K$ large enough such that the constant $C(K, \| e\|_{C^{0,\gamma}})\leq 2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts that one fixed quadrature grid makes the continuous and empirical losses relatively equivalent (factor 2) uniformly over all v with \|v\|_\cV \le M. The justification eq:generalization is only a per-function asymptotic statement (ratio tending to 1 as K \to \infty for a fixed e); it does not hold uniformly over the ball at any fixed K. Concrete obstruction: take a linear PDE in the framework whose exact solution u lies in \cV (a regime the paper explicitly relies on, e.g. manufactured Gaussian-mixture solutions), and any nonzero w \in \cV annihilated by the K collocation functionals (the kernel is nontrivial because \cV is infinite-dimensional, and \cR[w] \ne 0 by uniqueness). Then v = u + \eps w satisfies \|v\|_\cV \le M for small \eps, \hat L(v) = 0, but L(v) = (\eps^2/2)\|\cE[w]\|_{L^2}^2 + (\lambda\eps^2/2)\|\cB[w]\|_{L^2}^2 > 0, violating L(v) \le 2\hat L(v) for every grid; hence no such K(M) exists. In general, Hölder-bounded residuals can concentrate between (or on) grid points, so only an additive uniform error |\hat L(v) - L(v)| \le \eps(K,M) is available.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lemma by the uniform additive quadrature estimate \sup_{\|v\|_\cV \le M} |L(v) - \hat L(v)| \le \eps(K,M) with \eps(K,M) \to 0 as K \to \infty (valid for uniformly Hölder families once the hypotheses of ISSUE-004 are added), and rework the proof of thm:error_bound by choosing K so that \eps(K, 3\|u^\delta\|_\cV) \le \delta; the theorem's statements and convergence rates are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:error_bound applies the lemma to bound L(u_{K,\alpha}) by 2\hat L(u_{K,\alpha}) precisely in the regime \hat L \approx 0 where relative control fails, so the finite-K convergence guarantee (one of the paper's main advertised results) is unproven as written.
issues.title: Uniform two-sided quadrature equivalence over a \cV-ball (lem:added-1) is false, breaking the finite-K error bound
issues.why_classification: The false lemma must be replaced by a new (standard but nontrivial) uniform quadrature lemma and the dependent proof re-parameterized; this is a contained correction with no loss of the theorem statements or advertised rates, so it is more than minor but does not require new global architecture or cause major loss.
